edges.effect_quant: A small and mixed literature point in more than one direction, so no single pooled effect estimate is reliable enough to summarize cleanly.
edges.mechanism: Vitamin D signaling affects calcium handling, immune tone, renin-angiotensin activity, and skeletal muscle, but supplementation only changes those pathways meaningfully when baseline status is low. That helps explain why effects on Allergic disease are usually clearest in deficiency and muted in already replete adults.
edges.summary: Vitamin D supplementation in infancy appears tied to mixed effects on allergic disease in infants and young children mainly through a small and mixed literature. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
